title: What If Every Ant on Earth Vanished?

scenes.text: What if every ant vanished? You'd lose more living weight than all wild birds and mammals combined.
Roughly twenty quadrillion ants live on Earth, in nearly every habitat except the polar regions.
The soil would feel it first. Ants move up to thirteen tons of soil per hectare every year, cycling nutrients.
Plants would lose their gardeners too. Ants spread the seeds of many plants.
Forests and dry lands, where ants are most abundant, would feel the loss most.
Ants add up to about twenty percent of humanity's weight. Remove them, and the ground beneath forests would stop being turned.
